en.headline: Privacy Commissioner urges businesses to invest more in data security amid AI-assisted attacks
en.dek: Ada Chung said recent breaches affecting more than one million users show hackers are using AI to speed up attacks, and organisations must strengthen systems even when using third parties.
body: Privacy Commissioner Ada Chung Lai-ling urged business operators on Thursday to allocate more resources to strengthen information technology systems following a series of cybersecurity breaches that have affected more than one million users.

Chung said hackers are increasingly using artificial intelligence to launch attacks more quickly, as the technology removes the need for extensive online testing and lowers the barriers to carrying out attacks. She called on organisations to hire cybersecurity professionals and to take responsibility for data protection even when they engage third-party contractors.

The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data has noted an expansion in the range of sectors affected by breaches, from aviation and electrical retail to other retail and financial services. Chung's comments follow several high-profile incidents reported in recent weeks.

Organisations were advised to conduct regular vulnerability assessments, install timely software updates, use multi-factor authentication for remote access and ensure that personal data is not retained longer than necessary.

zh.headline: 私隱專員促企業加強資料保安投資 指黑客用AI加快攻擊
zh.dek: 鍾麗玲表示近期多宗事故影響逾百萬人，黑客借助人工智能加速入侵，機構即使外判亦須負責。
body: 個人資料私隱專員鍾麗玲今日促請商界營運者投放更多資源，強化資訊科技系統，以應對一連串影響超過一百萬名用戶的網絡保安事故。
鍾麗玲指出，黑客愈來愈多利用人工智能技術加快發動攻擊，因技術減少了網上測試的需要，並降低了攻擊的門檻。她呼籲機構聘請網絡保安專業人員，即使將系統外判予第三方，仍須對資料保護負責。
私隱專員公署留意到受影響行業範圍擴大，由航空及電器零售擴展至其他零售及金融業。她的言論是在近周多宗高調資料外洩事件後作出。
公署建議機構定期進行漏洞評估、及時安裝軟件更新、對遠端存取使用多重認證，並確保個人資料不會保存超過所需時間。
